newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia oppn to oppose woodchip export plan.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia oppn to oppose woodchip export plan.

text.p: Australian Labor opposition environment spokeswoman Carmen Lawrence said on Monday it would not support the government's new export regulations which allow an additional million tonnes of woodchips to be exported this year.
"The government's transitional forest policy is seriously flawed and we have major difficulties with technical aspects of the regulations," Lawrence said in a statement.
Lawrence said it would support the disallowance motion presented by the Australian Greens in the Senate, the upper house, last week to scrap the government's proposed regulations.
The government last Tuesday approved five more export licences for 1996 against the Greens' motion, allowing 415,000 tonnes of chips from native forests.
But since passage of a motion requires a majority of senators, Labor would need the support of all non-government members of the upper house to to disallow the regulations.
The two Independent senators have not said how they will vote.

"Increases in the woodchip export quota, the abolition of the two-stage licensing system, and the clearing of privately owned forests for woodchipping were not spelt out by the (Liberal-National) coalition at the last election and represent a major threat to the development of a genuinely sustainable forestry industry," Lawrence said.
The government said in July under the new export licencing regime exporters would have access to an additional one million tonnes of woodchips sourced exclusively from sawmill residues in 1996.
Primary Industries Minister John Anderson said the ceiling of 5.251 million tonnes applying to all woodchips would continue.
The system of first and second-stage licences would be abolished with three-year licences available from 1997.
Lawrence said the drafted regulations were technically inadequate.

"It is extraordinary that there is no definition of degraded forests and that the Environment Minister (Robert Hill) is to have no influence over the decision to permit the clearing of forests on private land..," she said.
